title: Verifier‑Grounded Generate‑Verify‑Repair for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Paired Mininet Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a provenance‑traced paired confirmatory study (N = 200 intents; 400 paired episodes) to evaluate whether a deterministic verifier‑grounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) loop reduces operationally detectable policy‑violation errors when a hosted LLM produces device configuration sequences from operator intent in a Mininet emulation. Execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial generation per intent reused by both baseline and guarded). Baseline success (no detected policy violation) = 196/200 (98%); guarded success = 200/200 (100%). Paired risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.02; preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.125 (primary confirmatory test). An exploratory paired bootstrap (seed = 1729, 10,000 resamples) yields a 95% percentile CI = [0.005, 0.04]. Four verifier‑triggered repairs occurred (total hosted model calls = 204), giving mean extra model calls per intent = 0.02 and mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0. All reported numeric values, provider‑call accounting, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are drawn verbatim from the archived execution and analysis bundle. We interpret the preregistered confirmatory result conservatively and discuss construct, internal, and external validity limits and operational implications.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation is an active NetOps research direction because it promises faster operator workflows and reduced manual error for routine maintenance. However, prior work shows that LLMs can produce mechanically detectable faults—syntax errors, reachability/topology violations, and ACL/policy mistakes—that may cause outages or expose resources [1], [4]. Generate–Verify‑Repair (GVR) architectures pair an LLM generator with a deterministic verifier that checks mechanizable constraints and, when violations occur, requests localized repairs from the model. Prototype and domain studies report reductions in mechanically checkable errors using verifier‑grounded repair in code and program generation contexts [2], [3].

We preregistered study C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1 to test whether a deterministic verifier plus bounded repair reduces operationally detectable policy violations produced by a hosted LLM across heterogeneous synthetic vendor templates and topology patterns in an emulator. To make paired inference robust and auditable, the experiment enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one sampled initial generation per intent reused by both baseline and guarded episodes) so any per‑pair improvement could only arise from deterministic validator and permitted repair actions, not from independent re‑sampling or alternative initial prompts. The preregistration preceded any model calls (SHA‑256 = 9e0fc992665835975b01289f7841926ef6abf3584252c5d0459ba0ecf166bb50).
sections.related_work:
Surveys and recent NetOps research document rapid growth of LLM applications for network configuration and AIOps while highlighting evaluation gaps: provenance, verifier integration, and realistic emulation evidence [5], [6]. NetConfEval and related prototype benchmarks demonstrate LLMs' promise for configuration drafting but also reveal frequent syntactic, topology, or policy errors when outputs are executed or emulated [4]. Complementary cross‑domain work on verifier‑guided repair and generate‑verify‑repair patterns shows measurable reductions in mechanically checkable errors for code and domain programs, though prior studies are typically single‑case or limited in task diversity [2], [3].

Our study situates itself at the intersection of these literatures by (i) using provenance‑traced paired inference in an emulator stratified over multiple synthetic vendor‑template families, (ii) enforcing shared_initial_candidate semantics so paired effects are attributable strictly to deterministic validator/repair behavior (not to different first‑pass samples), and (iii) reporting complete provider and verifier accounting to quantify concrete hosted‑LLM repair cost. We avoid claims beyond the emulation and synthetic template scope and do not claim production readiness or broad multi‑model generality.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The experiment was preregistered as C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1. The primary confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (probability that an intent yields zero operationally detectable violations under guarded minus baseline) tested via exact McNemar two‑sided test (α = 0.05). Exploratory estimators include a paired bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000) and descriptive cost metrics (mean extra hosted model calls per intent and mean extra calls per avoided violation). The preregistration and execution artifacts are archived and referenced in the execution manifest.

Sampling, task bank, and shared_initial_candidate semantics: N = 200 unique operator intents were deterministically selected and stratified across three synthetic vendor‑template families and four topology patterns (12 strata) according to the frozen task index profile. Execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics: exactly one initial sampled generation per intent was produced and reused by both baseline and guarded episodes. Under this design baseline outcome equals the deterministic validator verdict on that shared initial candidate; the guarded outcome equals the final guarded pipeline result after deterministic validation and any permitted repair. The preregistration explicitly defined that independent constrained‑prompt arms were not executed; therefore the paired comparison isolates validator/repair effects only.

Model, sampling notation, and budget accounting: The declared model in the archived model_configuration.json is gpt‑5‑mini (provider recorded as openai_responses). The archived configuration records temperature = null/unset; we explicitly state that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic provider sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Planned budget: planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_model_calls = 400. The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 204.

Deterministic validator and repair policy: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performs syntactic parsing, required‑command sequencing checks, emulated reachability/topology verification, and encoded ACL/policy checks derived from per‑task payload constraints. The validator returns a boolean success = "no detected violations" under the scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation. When violations are detected the guarded pipeline may issue up to one verifier‑triggered repair call; repair prompts were built from the validator's localized diagnostics to request corrective modifications. Validator traces (validation_before and validation_after), repair decisions, and whether repair_applied occurred are recorded per episode in the scoring artifacts.

Scoring, missingness, and analysis plan: The preregistration specified exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary success indicators as the formal confirmatory test. Missingness/exclusion rules were predeclared: deterministic duplicates, unrecoverable infrastructure failures, or ambiguous validator outputs would be handled conservatively (ambiguous outputs treated as violations in the primary analysis). The primary analysis uses the complete_pair_primary treatment; sensitivity analyses were predeclared to treat infrastructure failures conservatively as failures. In execution no pairs were excluded and no episodes failed.
sections.results:
Execution completeness and raw counts: The run completed per preregistration: planned_episode_count = 400; completed_episode_count = 400; complete_pair_count = 200; failed_episode_count = 0. The archived paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 196 (both succeed), n10 = 4 (guarded succeed, baseline fail), n01 = 0 (guarded fail, baseline succeed), n00 = 0 (both fail). Baseline success rate = 196/200 = 0.98; guarded success rate = 200/200 = 1.0; paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.02.

Confirmatory test and exploratory interval: The preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes yields p = 0.125 (primary confirmatory result; do not reject at α = 0.05). The archived exploratory paired bootstrap (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000) produced a 95% percentile CI for the paired risk difference = [0.005, 0.04]; the bootstrap seed and resampling parameters are archived in analysis_log.jsonl. Because discordant counts were small (n10 + n01 = 4), bootstrap percentile intervals can be unstable in this sparse regime; we therefore present the bootstrap CI as descriptive magnitude context while treating the exact McNemar p‑value as the preregistered confirmatory inference.

Repair accounting and provider audit: Deterministic_reconciliation and execution manifest provider_call_audit report hosted_model_call_event_count = 204 (completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 204; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; cache_hit_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 204). Stage_counts were shared_initial_generation = 200 and repair = 4; condition_counts recorded shared = 200 and guarded = 4 under the adapter's internal stage notation. These audited counts decompose as 200 shared initial generations (one per intent) plus 4 verifier‑triggered repair calls. From these figures mean hosted model calls per intent = 204/200 = 1.02 and mean extra calls per intent due to repairs = 0.02. Each repair corrected a baseline failure in the archived contingency, giving mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0. All provider accounting figures are verbatim from deterministic_reconciliation.json and execution_manifest.

Representative episodes and validator traces: Representative scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task‑000004‑*.json, task‑000005‑*, task‑000006‑*) show identical shared_initial_candidate content and identical baseline and guarded shared_initial responses (the shared initial text was reused by both conditions). For the discordant pairs the validator_trace.validation_before recorded the detected violation, repair_applied = true in the corresponding guarded trace, and validator_trace.validation_after recorded final_configuration passing full_intent_constraint_validation. These per‑episode artifacts substantiate the contingency table and the repair accounting reported above.

Statistical diagnostics and power context: The preregistered power plan targeted a 10 percentage point absolute reduction with N ≈ 157 (McNemar approximation); N = 200 was chosen to permit stratified descriptions. The observed baseline failure prevalence (2%) was lower than some sensitivity scenarios used in planning, reducing power to detect small absolute improvements and explaining the nonsignificant McNemar result despite a positive point estimate. Given the small number of discordant pairs, effect magnitude estimates should be interpreted cautiously.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics: Because the experiment executed the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one sampled initial generation per intent reused by baseline and guarded), any paired improvement derives solely from deterministic validator/repair actions rather than from independent first‑pass re‑sampling or alternative prompts. The preregistration explicitly declared that constrained‑prompt arms were not executed; readers should not attribute the guarded improvement to prompt engineering or to different initial generations.

Operational meaning and bounded claims: Within the constrained Mininet emulation, synthetic vendor templates, and the validator's encoded rule set, a small repair budget (four repairs) removed all mechanically detectable baseline violations observed in this task bank. This artifact‑grounded outcome indicates that, where a deterministic verifier can express and check the operational constraints of interest and produce localized diagnostics, bounded repair budgets can eliminate mechanically checkable faults in template‑driven emulated settings. These results do not establish production readiness, multi‑model generality, or coverage for higher‑order semantic misinterpretations outside the validator's rule coverage.

Threats to validity (summary): Construct validity—the deterministic validator covers syntactic, reachability/topology, and encoded ACL/policy checks but cannot detect higher‑order semantic misunderstandings not expressible in its rules. Internal validity—shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced and verified in deterministic_reconciliation.json, preventing attribution of paired gains to different initial samples. Conclusion validity—small discordant counts limit the power for detecting small absolute effects and make resampling intervals less stable; the exact McNemar test is the preregistered confirmatory procedure. External validity—single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic templates, and Mininet emulation limit generalization to production hardware, other prompt families, and different hosted model versions.

Artifact‑grounded recommendations: (1) Broaden deterministic verifier rule coverage to encode more semantic and policy ontologies and measure residual false negatives using targeted injection tests; (2) run paired designs with independent multi‑sample initial generations (not executed here) to isolate prompt/template effects versus verifier effects; (3) evaluate multiple hosted models and versions to assess robustness to provider nondeterminism; (4) preserve provenance tracing (provider calls, validator traces, and task manifests) for independent audit and reproducibility. Each recommendation follows directly from archived evidence and observed limitations.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a provenance‑traced paired confirmatory study (N = 200 intents; shared_initial_candidate semantics) to measure whether a deterministic verifier plus bounded repair reduces mechanically detectable policy violations in intent→configuration tasks in a Mininet emulation. The preregistered exact McNemar two‑sided test did not reject at α = 0.05 (p = 0.125). Guarded GVR invoked four repairs and corrected the observed baseline violations at low model‑call overhead (mean extra calls per intent = 0.02), yielding a paired risk difference estimate of 0.02 and an exploratory paired bootstrap CI = [0.005, 0.04] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000). These artifact‑grounded results indicate that, when a deterministic verifier can express and check relevant constraints and provide localized feedback, a small repair budget can eliminate mechanically detectable policy violations in similar template‑based emulated settings. Future preregistered, provenance‑traced evaluations should expand verifier coverage, evaluate multiple hosted models, and compare independent multi‑sample baselines.

disclosure_statement: Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (provider recorded as openai_responses). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration: C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1 (SHA‑256 = 9e0fc992665835975b01289f7841926ef6abf3584252c5d0459ba0ecf166bb50) was recorded before any model calls. Initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role: a human Research Director selected the topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; after the autonomy lock the AI autonomously performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, revision, and manuscript drafting; no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Sampling semantics: execution used shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per intent was produced and reused by both baseline and guarded); archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset (null/unset is not evidence of deterministic provider sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). Provider accounting (audited): hosted_model_call_event_count = 204 decomposed as 200 shared initial generations + 4 repair calls. Reported numbers and analysis artifacts are drawn from the archived execution and analysis bundles.
limitations: Scope limited to Mininet‑style emulation with synthetic, provenance‑traced intent→configuration tasks; results do not generalize directly to production hardware or live operations.
Single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) evaluated; multi‑model generality is not established.

Deterministic validator coverage limited to mechanically checkable errors (syntax, reachability, ACL/policy encodings); higher‑level semantic or specification misinterpretations outside the validator may remain undetected.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics imply observed paired differences derive only from verifier‑triggered repair; this design does not measure effects of alternative prompting strategies or independent multi‑sample candidate selection.

Observed confirmatory effect (2 percentage points) did not reach statistical significance at α = 0.05 for N = 200 (exact McNemar p = 0.125); low baseline failure prevalence (2%) reduced power to detect small absolute improvements under some preregistered scenarios.
